newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends switch-backed ride off lows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends switch-backed ride off lows.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended Thursday lower but off lows after a choppy session dominated by nearby switches, traders said.
Values were earlier depressed by long liquidation and origin selling in the back months.
But a rebound in New York arabica futures and good trade and industry buying underneath as well as persistent arbitrage buying against the U.S. market lifted prices from intraday lows.
"New York is currently in positive figures and looking reasonably strong," said one trader.
"Dec/March traded up to eight (U.S.) cents as well which will keep the market reasonably steady for the time being," the trader added.
Most-active January was $17 lower on the day to finish at $1,471 a tonne, off a low of $1,459.
Front-month November was $26 down at $1,523, just above an immediate support of $1,520.
Volume was 4,386 lots. Of these, about 1,000 lots were Nov/Jan switches and a big chunk of 500 lots was traded at $63.
"The funds are obviously rolling shorts forward," one said.
By the close, the Nov/Jan spread narrowed to $52 from Wednesday's $61 finish. The widening December premium over March in New York reflected the tight nearby coffee supplies in the U.S.

U.S. certified coffee stocks are at the lowest levels since mid-1980s and are in firm hands while newly-harvested Central and South American beans are not due to reach Western markets at least until early December.
Mexico said its crop could be delayed due to heavy rains while there were also reports that Guatemala and Costa Rica could also face crop delays.
The next U.S. and U.K. certified stocks are due late on Monday and Tuesday respectively.
